title: Symmetry Origins of the Field-Free Superconducting Diode Effect in the Kagome Superconductor CsV$_3$Sb$_5$
authors: Xin-Jie Liu, Shengbiao Sun, Ke-Fan Song, Jia-Peng Peng, Xilin Feng, Lang Xiao, Tong Liu, Qilin Han, Ya-Qing Bie, Ning Kang, Xiaosong Wu, Yanfei Wu, Shouguo Wang, Kam Tuen Law, Shuo Wang, Dapeng Yu, Ben-Chuan Lin
abstract: Field-free superconducting diode effects require both inversion-symmetry breaking and an internal time-reversal-symmetry (TRS) breaking field, making them sensitive probes of hidden order in superconductors. In centrosymmetric kagome AV$_3$Sb$_5$, the inversion symmetry generally should generally preclude the observation of the superconducting diode effect. Furthermore, though TRS breaking has been reported in the superconducting regime of CsV$_3$Sb$_5$, whether it is generated by superconductivity or inherited from charge-density-wave (CDW) order remains unresolved. Here we show that pristine CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ devices exhibit no intrinsic field-free superconducting diode effect, whereas surface oxidation or asymmetric etching activates a large nonreciprocal supercurrent. Moreover, the response is stochastic, with sweep-dependent polarity and magnitude, indicating metastable TRS-breaking domain configurations. Small out-of-plane magnetic fields stabilize the superconducting diode response, consistent with field selection of such domains. Finally, when long-range CDW order is suppressed by Ti doping, the SDE disappears. Our results establish the symmetry requirements for the field-free SDE in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$, reveal its stochastic domain-controlled character, and link superconducting-state TRS breaking to CDW-related order.
summary: This experimental work investigates the superconducting diode effect in CsV3Sb5, finding that the effect only appears when inversion symmetry is externally broken. Crucially, the authors link this non-reciprocal supercurrent to the presence of charge-density-wave order, demonstrating that suppressing the CDW order eliminates the diode effect.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin and symmetry requirements for the field-free superconducting diode effect (SDE) in the Kagome superconductor CsV3Sb5.
main_result: The SDE requires extrinsic inversion symmetry breaking and is linked to time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking associated with the charge-density-wave (CDW) order, as its disappearance upon CDW suppression confirms this link.
method: The authors performed transport measurements (dI/dV) on fabricated devices, systematically inducing symmetry breaking via surface oxidation or asymmetric etching, and comparing results with doped samples.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Kagome superconductor CsV3Sb5, which is centrosymmetric. The study probes the superconducting state's response to symmetry breaking, particularly focusing on the interplay between inversion symmetry, TRS, and CDW order.
key_observables:
Diode asymmetry parameter ($\eta$), nonreciprocal supercurrent ($	ext{I}_{c+} 
eq 	ext{I}_{c-}$), and the stability of the diode response under applied magnetic fields.
important_parameters: Temperature (low T, e.g., 1.8 K), applied magnetic fields (out-of-plane and in-plane), and the degree of CDW order (controlled by Ti doping).
main_assumptions: The initial pristine state is assumed to be centrosymmetric and thus diode-inactive; the stochastic nature is interpreted as arising from metastable domain configurations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the induction of SDE via oxidation/etching, show the stochastic nature of the response across multiple sweeps, demonstrate field stabilization of the diode polarity, and confirm the loss of SDE upon Ti doping.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the baseline (pristine, no SDE), then demonstrates the activation of SDE through controlled symmetry breaking (oxidation/etching). It characterizes the stochastic nature and field dependence, and finally confirms the underlying physical mechanism by showing the SDE vanishes when the CDW order is suppressed by doping.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed experimental test of symmetry protection in superconductivity, linking macroscopic transport phenomena (diode effect) to microscopic electronic orders (CDW) and symmetry breaking mechanisms.
